children: Australia’s seasonally adjusted unemployment rate stood at 4.7% in September, unchanged from an upwardly revised figure in August and above expectations of 4.6%.
It was the highest since October 2021, with the number of unemployed increasing by 8,900 to 732,000, the highest since April 2021.

Meanwhile, employment unexpectedly fell by 39,300 to 14.78 million, defying expectations for a rise of 20,000, following a downwardly revised increase of 29,300 jobs in August. Part-time employment declined by 73,700 to 4.55 million, while full-time employment increased by 34,400 to 10.23 million.
The participation rate edged down to 66.8% from 67.0% in August, coming in above expectations and reaching its lowest level in four months.
Meanwhile, the underemployment rate inched up to 6.3% from 6.2% in August, while total monthly hours worked across all jobs increased by 1 million to 2.011 billion.

title: Australia Jobless Rate Holds at Nearly 5-Year High
